entries.details: See {IGovernor-hashProposal}. The proposal id is produced by hashing the ABI encoded `targets` array, the `values` array, the `calldatas` array and the descriptionHash (bytes32 which itself is the keccak256 hash of the description string). This proposal id can be produced from the proposal data which is part of the {ProposalCreated} event. It can even be computed in advance, before the proposal is submitted. Note that the chainId and the governor address are not part of the proposal id computation. Consequently, the same proposal (with same operation and same description) will have the same id if submitted on multiple governors across multiple networks. This also means that in order to execute the same operation twice (on the same governor) the proposer will have to change the description in order to avoid proposal id conflicts.

IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction ordering also applies here. Emits an {Approval} event. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future. - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner` over the EIP712-formatted function arguments. - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}). entries.notice: Return a proposal's immutable execution start.

returns._0: Inclusive lower bound of the proposal execution window, or zero for a nonexistent proposal.

entries.notice: Return a proposal's immutable creation-time expiry.

returns._0: Exclusive upper bound of the proposal execution window, or zero for a nonexistent proposal.

entries.notice: Return whether a proposal needs an external queue transaction.
entries.details: Direct callers always receive false: creation snapshots the complete execution window and the queue selector is not installed. OpenZeppelin 5.7 validates `execute` against exactly one state. While this facet's `execute` implementation delegates to that validation, report true so its documented time-gated `Queued` presentation is accepted. The facet has already validated the immutable execution window before delegation.

returns._0: Whether the inherited execute path must validate `Queued` state.

entries.details: The account that created a proposal.

entries.notice: module:core
entries.details: Timepoint used to retrieve user's votes and quorum. If using block number (as per Compound's Comp), the snapshot is performed at the end of this block. Hence, voting for this proposal starts at the beginning of the following block.

entries.notice: Return proposal threshold.

returns._0: Minimum voting power required to create a proposal.

entries.notice: Return the current proposal-threshold numerator.

returns._0: Threshold numerator expressed over one billion.

entries.notice: Return proposal votes.

params.proposalId: Proposal whose accumulated vote totals are returned.

entries.notice: Return current CYGLD custody, allowance exposure, and aggregate commitment.

entries.details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`.
Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

entries.notice: Return the Safe wallet used for emergency authority.

returns._0: Configured Safe-wallet address.

entries.notice: Replace the execution delay when its current value matches the caller's expectation.
entries.details: Callable only by Governance executing a proposal against itself. No-op rejection precedes stale-current rejection; the replacement must remain within the compiled 1-to-30-day bounds. Existing proposals retain their creation-time execution windows.

params.currentExecutionDelay: Caller-expected execution delay, in timestamp seconds.
params.newExecutionDelay: Replacement execution delay, in timestamp seconds.

entries.notice: Replace the execution grace period when its current value matches the caller's expectation.
entries.details: Callable only by Governance executing a proposal against itself. No-op rejection precedes stale-current rejection; the replacement must remain within the compiled 1-to-30-day bounds. Existing proposals retain their creation-time execution windows.

params.currentExecutionGracePeriod: Caller-expected execution-window length, in timestamp seconds.
params.newExecutionGracePeriod: Replacement execution-window length, in timestamp seconds.

entries.notice: Replace the threshold numerator when its current value matches the caller's expectation.
entries.details: Callable only by Governance executing a proposal against itself. No-op rejection precedes stale-current rejection; the replacement must remain within the compiled bounds. The change affects proposals created after this transaction.

entries.notice: Replace the quorum numerator when its current value matches the caller's expectation.
entries.details: Callable only by Governance executing a proposal against itself. No-op rejection precedes stale-current rejection; the replacement must remain between 1 and 50 inclusive. The change affects proposals created after this transaction.

entries.notice: Replace the configured Safe wallet using compare-and-set semantics.

params.expectedCurrentSafeWallet: Safe wallet expected to be configured before the update.
params.newSafeWallet: Contract with a nonempty, unique owner roster and a sane execution threshold.

entries.notice: Replace the voting delay when its current value matches the caller's expectation.

params.currentVotingDelay: Caller-expected current voting delay, in timestamp seconds.
params.newVotingDelay: Replacement voting delay, in timestamp seconds.

entries.notice: Replace the voting period when its current value matches the caller's expectation.

params.currentVotingPeriod: Caller-expected current voting period, in timestamp seconds.
params.newVotingPeriod: Replacement voting period, in timestamp seconds.

entries.notice: Query if a contract implements an interface
entries.details: Interface identification is specified in ERC-165. This function  uses less than 30,000 gas.

params.interfaceId: The interface identifier, as specified in ERC-165

returns._0: `true` if the contract implements `interfaceID` and  `interfaceID` is not 0xffffffff, `false` otherwise

entries.details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

entries.notice: Return the Governance diamond itself as the CYGOV voting token.

returns._0: Governance diamond implementing IERC5805 through TokenFacet.

entries.details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.
See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

entries.notice: Transfer an exact ERC-20 amount from Governance treasury custody.
entries.details: Requires `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, is unavailable while Governance is paused, and is nonreentrant. For CYGLD, the transfer must preserve all Recovery Fund commitments and allowance exposure. Zero amount is a no-op after both addresses are validated; fee-on-transfer short credit reverts atomically.

params.amount: Amount to transfer, in the token's base units.
params.to: Nonzero account that must receive the exact amount.
params.token: ERC-20 token held by the Governance diamond.
